digital_typology.purpose: Define and construct a minimal, coarse project memory graph shape for the target by identifying its categorical notable elements and joining them through type specific Operative Purposes.

core_concepts.concept: The actual thing being examined, created, or used. Artifacts can include photographs, contracts, stories, resale assets, and software. The work can concern multiple artifacts and projects. Whether an artifact serves as an asset depends on its use in that context.

An entity that is capable of being named, identified, or worthy of note within the understanding of an artifact.
Entities are elements, joins are elements, not all elements are entities. An element is a namable thing of consideration, while entities are objects which are in the elements under consideration.

A dictionary object that exists in the RE with a relation in active voice, an observation as an atomic fact that is present in all artifacts of its type; additionally it contains a dictionary of objects containing type specific or artifact specific references and logic.

The "who" or "what" bearing an OP. This is the person, group, system, component, or other participant with an Operative Purpose for the Encounter Function of an Element. The OP belongs to that receiver.

The "how" description. This is the mechanism, interface, relationship, or method through which an Artifact or Element performs its purpose for its Receiving Entity. It explains how the effect is encountered, used, or experienced.

The unique scope of all Elements, excluding Elements that answer to who, Parametric Elements, and the actual reified joins.
code document media data

The "why." This is the active why an encounter function is meant to satisfy. This represents the JOIN between elements in the graph. It is the only element in the graph which can speak directly to the artifact; all other elements must speak to a common encounter function type which may be understood in many artifacts, not just this one.
An element of this artifact whose categorical role must be named in order to understand the minimal shape.

The notable element of this artifact whose loss would prevent the artifact from remaining the same type. Its Encounter Function summarizes the combined result of the artifact being examined. Its defining function is expressed independently of medium, encoding, genre, and style.
Any notable element of this artifact which is entangled with the encounter of the Defining Element in such a way that if omitted, the artifact would not remain the same type.
Any element which exists in the full cached namespace enumerated from the Native Metaform, or the Inference Metaform (recursively enumerated from aliases and joins in the Native Metaform) itself.

namespace_rules.rule: For each dotted part, the address in the namespace must be reversible and read as its name.
Namespace entries must describe the type of functional approach.
To be placed into the namespace, an entry must be the same thing as its parent type, or a function within its parent type, without being a non-functionality based variant.
Children must take their parent's name as their last name when reversed and read as a noun.
Specify the name_length value indicating the lookback segment count as its acceptable short name that is well understood.
The segments in the namespace can be reversed by replacing periods with spaces to read properly as an inferenceable, well understood name.
It must be a part or type of its parent scope.
Namespace must narrow from trunk to leaf.
namespace_rules.note: This is a typological ontology, it is not a taxonomy. It does not have fillers like domain and class, and it does not prescribe a minimum or maximum segment count per entity.

method.step: Find each notable element as a requirement.
Name this element's OP in the join which leads to it.
Once complete, move to the next element and treat it as the RE.
Continue until there are no more notable elements of this artifact that must be named to understand the artifact.
Anneal and combine elements when the shape can logically be reduced without losing the minimal categorical understanding of the artifact.
Only combine elements when they can logically share a common join.
When combining elements, seek a common element name that can be placed in the namespace and that adheres to the namespace naming rules while logically containing the combined elements.

When elements are combined away into a common element, the join may contain a dictionary of the entities combined away, with each entry expressed as: the combined element, a relation in the active voice, and an observation as an atomic fact.

List the subtypes you annealed away as subtypes, each a full namespace address beneath the element it was combined into. These subtypes are not part of the intake Metaform; they are held for the next steps as detected inactive subtypes, valid for memories to be attached to or to be named as namespace addresses. Their dependencies belong to the main type.

digital_typology.goal: Create a base shape that can be directly resolved to contain project memory graph relations and other knowledge layers that can expand this shape. This is meant to be a shallow operation that forms a shape of notable elements which can later be extended with additional information. It is important to realize that the goal is to establish a set of base elements as reference points that can contain regional knowledge in the project. Seeking to perform a deep intake will only hurt the project and may segment information away from the area an agent addresses as a reference. It is imperative to recognize the load-bearing nature of this statement and of this operation as a whole.

constraints.constraint: Elements represent discrete functional roles actively instantiated by this artifact, named and described at their most specific reusable type level.
Never use vague top-level labels where a specific functional mechanism exists.
Keep all artifact-specific instance data strictly confined to the Operative Purpose.
After working through the process, attempt to anneal joins and combine elements to a final shape that speaks to the artifact type.
Treat the elements as elements of this artifact, joined by artifact-specific OP.
Keep the graph shape minimal, coarse, shallow, and extensible.
You must combine elements when doing so is logical and supports annealing into general specific shape.
Where elements are combined away, the join must preserve them as a dictionary of entities using active-voice relations and atomic observations.

digital_typology.completion_condition: The task is complete when the final result is a minimal base shape of notable categorical elements of the artifact, joined by artifact-specific Operative Purposes, suitable for later expansion through project memory graph relations and other knowledge layers.

response_instructions.instruction: Respond only in well-formed XML. Do not include prose, markdown, or commentary outside the XML document.
Use the tag set defined in response_schema below as the required output structure. Do not invent alternate tag names for the same concepts.
Every element must declare a role attribute of DE, SE, PE, or NE.
Every namespace attribute must be a dotted address that satisfies namespace_rules above.
Every join must express re, ef_ref, op, relation, and observation.
Artifact-specific instance data must appear only inside op elements, never inside ef or re elements.
Combined-away entities must be listed inside combined_entities within the join that absorbed them, each with its own relation and observation.
Annealed-away subtypes must be listed inside the subtypes block, each as a full namespace address beneath its parent element.
Keep the graph minimal, coarse, and shallow: only include elements required to understand the artifact's type. Do not perform a deep intake.

join.re: [id of the element bearing the OP]
join.ef_ref: [id of the element or shared EF type this join connects]
join.observation: [atomic fact true of all artifacts of this type]

subtype.namespace: [full dotted address beneath its parent element]
